## Design note

The theatre car. A screaming twelve, scissor doors and a body wider than a delivery van make it the loudest thing in any race. The automated manual thumps every shift and costs a few tenths against the dual-clutch cars, but the AWD launch and the V12's top end keep it on terms with anything on a long road. Heavy and wide in traffic: it does not like tight gaps.

## How this car breaks

Carbon tub with aluminium front and rear subframes. The very long rear deck carries the V12 and gearbox on the rear subframe, so rear hits kill drive; the nose holds the front diff and twin radiators in a short crush zone. The scissor doors hinge at the A-pillar base and tear off in side hits. Wide carbon bodywork shatters on any contact and is ruinous to replace.

## Inertia

Box approximation about the CG, scaled for mass concentration (`k < 1`: mass near the centre, e.g. mid-engine; `k → 1`: mass at the ends):

```
I_roll  = k_r · m·(W² + H²)/12
I_pitch = k_p · m·(L² + H²)/12
I_yaw   = k_y · m·(W² + L²)/12
```

| roll | 764 | 0.78 | 600 |
| pitch | 3404 | 0.76 | 2590 |

## Engine

6.5 L DOHC 48-valve 60° V12, naturally aspirated, dry sump, variable intake and exhaust cam phasing. Class-typical 2010s NA 6.5 V12 flagship (~79 kW/L, ~516 kW at 8250 rpm, 690 N·m at 5500) per manufacturer spec-class data and owner dyno sheets; a long, flat torque curve with a big crank and flywheel (highest engine inertia of the supercars).

## Drivetrain

7-speed single-clutch automated manual (robotised, hydraulic actuation; the slowest shift of the supercars), permanent AWD with a viscous-type centre coupling modelled as a fixed 25 % front split, clutch-type rear LSD. Layout **AWD, 25 % front**; front diff: open; rear diff: clutch LSD, preload 60 N·m, power ramp 0.45, coast ramp 0.30. Clutch capacity 1.40 × peak torque = 970 N·m. Shift time 0.22 s.

| Gear | Ratio | Overall | km/h @ redline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 3.91 | 13.37 | 80 |
| 2 | 2.44 | 8.34 | 128 |
| 3 | 1.81 | 6.19 | 172 |
| 4 | 1.46 | 4.99 | 214 |
| 5 | 1.19 | 4.07 | 262 |
| 6 | 0.97 | 3.32 | 321 |
| 7 | 0.83 | 2.84 | 376 |

Final drive 3.42, reverse 2.90. Speeds use the driven-wheel loaded radius 0.333 m.

## Suspension

Springs from ride frequency, `k = m_s·(2πf)²` with sprung corner mass `m_s = axle load/2 − unsprung`; dampers `c = 2ζ·√(k·m_s)`, ζ = 0.32 bump, rebound = 1.5 × bump.

| Axle | m_s | f | Wheel rate k | Bump c | Rebound c | Travel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Front | 340 kg | 1.95 Hz | 51000 N/m | 2660 N·s/m | 3990 N·s/m | 0.11 m |
| Rear | 454 kg | 2.15 Hz | 82900 N/m | 3930 N·s/m | 5900 N·s/m | 0.12 m |

Anti-roll bars from a roll-gradient target of 1.5°/g with 52% of roll stiffness at the front. Roll arm h − h_rc = 0.327 m (roll centres 0.08 m F / 0.12 m R). Required total K_φ = m·g·arm/φ = 207386 N·m/rad; springs give k·t²/2 = 75424 F / 116936 R N·m/rad; bars supply the rest as `arb_n_per_m = K_bar/t²` = **11000 F / 0 R N/m** (clamped at ≥ 0). Resulting gradient 1.4°/g, front share 48%. Bump stops 200000 N/m.

Alignment: camber -1.3° F / -1.7° R, toe +0.00° F / +0.20° R (+ = in), caster 7.0°.

## Brakes

Full-pedal line pressure 100 bar.

- Front: 400 mm disc, pistons per side 40 mm + 38 mm + 34 mm → A = 33.0 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 175 mm, pad μ = 0.45: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.45·100 bar·33.0 cm²·0.175 m = **5195 N·m**
- Rear: 380 mm disc, pistons per side 38 mm + 34 mm → A = 20.4 cm², r_eff = D/2 − 25 mm = 165 mm, pad μ = 0.43: T = 2·μ·p·A·r_eff = 2·0.43·100 bar·20.4 cm²·0.165 m = **2898 N·m**

ABS ceiling: caliper capacity 5195 / 2898 N·m exceeds 1.5 × the front lock torque on this car's tire (peak μ 1.20), which `wp_vehicle`'s ABS cannot modulate (it releases to a fraction of the commanded torque, so an oversized caliper keeps the wheel locked). Both axles scaled by 0.54 → **2820 / 1570 N·m**. Remove when 02's ABS modulates relative to lock torque.

Lock check at 1 g on μ = 1 (load transfer m·a·h/L): front needs 1567 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.80×), rear needs 1175 N·m/wheel (capacity 1.34×).

`wp_vehicle` gives the axle `bias_front` favours its full `max_torque_*` and scales the other by (1 − b)/b, so `max_torque_*` holds the caliper capacity per wheel and `bias_front` acts as the proportioning valve: the rear is trimmed to the same lock margin as the front (ideal rear = T_f · lock_r/lock_f = 2114 N·m), never boosted above its caliper capacity. Rear capacity is below that (hardware-limited rear), so `bias_front` = **0.5**: both axles get full caliper torque → delivered 2820 N·m front / 1570 N·m rear per wheel at full pedal. Handbrake 2450 N·m per rear wheel.

## Steering

Ratio 14.5:1. Kerb-to-kerb turning circle 12.5 m → outer-front path radius 6.12 m, rear-axle-centre radius 4.63 m → mean road-wheel lock δ = atan(L/R) = **0.527 rad (30.2°)** (outer 26.2°, inner 35.6° at full Ackermann; `ackermann_frac` 0.50). Rack speed 1.6 rad/s.

## Damage lattice (`data/lattices/ombra_v12.json`)

289 nodes, 1853 beams, 6 detachables, 21 component mounts.

- Generated with `gen-lattice --id ombra_v12 --profile coupe --width 2.03 --length 4.78 --height 1.14 --wheelbase 2.7 --mass 338.3 --car-mass 1691.5 --clearance 0.11 --front-overhang 1.05 --strength 1.0` (20% of vehicle mass in the lattice; strength from durability class 3).
- Era `2010s`: gen-lattice's default HSS passenger cell kept as is.
- Carbon-fibre monocoque tub (stiffer than an HSS cell): 384 passenger-cell beams (cabin, sills, pillars, roof rails, cross-members) × 1.20 section.
- Aluminium body: 663 outer-panel beams mild_steel → aluminum.
- Mid-engine: engine block moved behind the cabin bulkhead (y -0.93…-1.58 m), mounted to the rear rails and the bulkhead; 10 nodes behind the bulkhead relabelled FrameRear (engine bay, not cabin); 16 front-rail beams × 1.6 (no engine block in the nose: they get gen-lattice's rear-rail factor); 194 rear-subframe beams → aluminum ×1.5 section (sacrificial); gearbox and half-shafts at the rear axle, side fuel tanks at the sills behind the seats; engine fails at 0.12 m, gearbox 0.08 m.
